active.text: Northeast winds 20 to 30 mph with gusts around 55 mph expected until 4 PM EST this afternoon. Anyone traveling on Thanksgiving Day should pay close attention to the latest conditions; downed trees combined with heavy rain may make travel dangerous at times.

readiness.hed: Fredericksburg wakes up to a wet, windy Thanksgiving Day near 58 with a Wind Advisory running until 4 p.m., rain tapers to a 50% chance overnight near 45, then Friday turns drier and breezier near 55 before a clear, sunny stretch builds in for the weekend near 61 Saturday and 62 Sunday
readiness.insight: The National Weather Service's Wind Advisory for the Fredericksburg region now runs from 4:29 a.m. to 4 p.m. EST today, Thanksgiving Day itself, for northeast winds of 20 to 30 mph with gusts around 55 mph — the Service specifically warns that anyone traveling to Thanksgiving dinner should watch conditions closely, since downed trees combined with heavy rain may make travel dangerous. Rain continues through the day with a high near 58 and a 100% chance of precipitation, with 2 to 3 inches of rainfall possible by evening. Tonight's rain chance drops to 50% with patchy fog and a low near 45, and Friday turns drier and breezier with a high near 55 under partly sunny skies. The weekend clears out nicely, with Saturday sunny near 61 and Sunday mostly sunny near 62.
actions: The Wind Advisory runs until 4 p.m. today — build in extra time for any Thanksgiving travel and watch for downed limbs or standing water on the roads.
Rain and gusts to 51 mph are expected most of the day — secure any outdoor turkey-fryer setup, decorations or seating before heading out this morning.
Keep devices charged and a flashlight handy in case gusty winds cause flickers or brief outages during dinner.
If your plans stretch into the evening, the rain chance drops to 50% overnight with patchy fog — allow extra time for the drive home.
